persona: IT Operations Lead at a mid-size IT services company, owns the SaaS tool stack, vendor renewals and tooling governance, and files cleanup work into Jira.
shared_context: All three runs read the same SaaS tracker, SSO report, renewal quotes, and governance policy, correctly reconciled every one of the 20 tracker rows, computed the same USD 140,340 total spend and USD 56,220 total saving, filed the same four Jira tickets (Slack to Microsoft Teams, Asana and Trello to Jira, Toggl Track to Harvest, Dropbox Business to OneDrive) plus the Pipedrive to HubSpot opportunity recorded on the tracker only, left Figma, Adobe XD, and Loom unresolved rather than guessing, posted a live Teams summary, and created five blank-recipient Gmail drafts with no cancellation, licence change, or vendor contact anywhere. Where they diverge is run time, labelling clarity in the tracker's decision column, how cleanly the citation trail separates sourced figures from added planning language, and whether every claimed figure actually appears somewhere else in the record to check it against.
suggested_field6_reason: The deliverable is complete and correct everywhere I checked it against the real source, the tracker, the tickets, the live post, and the drafts agree with each other and with the policy, and nothing was guessed where the policy gave no answer.

overall_task_success.commentary: The deliverable is complete and correct everywhere I checked it against the real source, the tracker, the tickets, the live post, and the drafts agree with each other and with the policy, and nothing was guessed where the policy gave no answer. What holds this at 5/7 rather than higher is that the tickets carry planning content past what was actually authorised for this review, stated with more certainty than the analysis and planning scope supports, alongside a small consistency gap in how retained standards are recorded. Neither one changes the underlying recommendations, which are sound and ready to act on, but a persona relying on this record would want the ticket scope trimmed back before treating it as final.

task_accuracy.commentary: Every number I checked against the source lands correctly, including both planted boundary cases, the renewal sitting exactly on the freeze cutoff and the quote converted from a foreign currency for the complementary whiteboarding tool, and the grouped project management opportunity is correctly tested as a combined figure. Two things keep this off a higher number. The record column for retained standards is not applied consistently, three carry a plain note that no ticket applies while a fourth adds a reference back to a different ticket for no clear structural reason. Separately, one ticket's added planning notes describe a migration in the next cycle using language more definite than the review actually authorised, which was analysis and planning only.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: none, no failed step or redo anywhere in the run
efficiency.commentary: This moved in a straight line from source review through reconciliation, ticket filing, the tracker write back, and the channel post without circling back on anything. The one real drag, small but visible in its own narration, is that the five department drafts were not created together, two went in first and the remaining three followed as a second round instead of one pass covering all five. It cost very little given the overall pace, but it is a genuine instance of work that could have been done together and was not, which is why this stops short of the top of the range.

writing_quality.commentary: The channel summary reads clearly, a short basis line up front followed by grouped headers for the filed opportunities, the calls flagged as higher risk, and the item recorded on the tracker only, so a reader can scan it in seconds. The Gmail drafts read naturally and each one closes with the required line noting a verified address is needed, without sounding boilerplate. Two things pull this back from a higher score. The Jira ticket bodies run long, with a section on planning scope on top of the required tools, target, and saving that makes each one longer than it needs to be for something meant to be actioned quickly. The channel post also restates the same dollar figures twice, once in the opportunity list and again in the risk section, adding nothing new the second time.

instruction_following.commentary: Every explicit constraint on the sheet, the channel, and the mailbox is honoured, the post is live rather than a draft, every email has a blank recipient field with the required note, and no subscription, licence, or vendor was touched. Rows with no policy answer were logged as unresolved rather than guessed. Two things keep this off a higher number. The ticket content was asked to name the tools covered, the tool being kept, and the saving, and instead each one adds a full planning section, inventory steps, access validation, rollback planning, that goes beyond the saving into effectively scoping a migration project this review was never asked to authorise. That same block appears in near identical form across all four tickets regardless of how different the opportunities are, reading like a standard addition rather than guidance built for each case.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none, the run completed unattended from start to finish
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: the planning scope sections in the tickets would need trimming back to the requested fields before filing them as is
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: It ran without needing a single interjection, and its closing channel message lists specific reconciled facts rather than a vague summary, the spend total, the saving split, the ticket numbers, and the unresolved rows are all named individually. That is real verification of the content itself, not just confirming actions fired. What it did not catch is that its own added planning language in the tickets sits slightly past the boundary limiting this review to analysis, a boundary the same tickets explicitly cite in their own closing line, a case of stating the guardrail correctly while still drifting past it in the same document.

citation_quality.commentary: The seat and saving arithmetic is shown as an actual calculation in each ticket rather than just asserted, so I could rebuild every number myself from the identity counts and the spare capacity shown inline. Two things keep it from the top mark. The policy sections behind each decision are cited specifically, but the identity numbers themselves are never tied to which specific report column they came from with the same precision, an asymmetry between how rigorously the two source types are cited. The added planning recommendations in the tickets are also written in the same confident, cited tone as the sourced figures, so nothing visually separates a grounded number from the model's own suggested next step.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: The gradable portion here is the email drafting itself, which happened on screen, since the sheet, ticket, and channel work went through direct tool calls rather than clicking through a page. Every draft carries the correct blank recipient field and the right department targeting, so nothing landed in the wrong place. The screen state itself has two small rough edges, compose windows were left stacked open on top of each other rather than closed one at a time, and a browser notification prompt is still sitting on screen, undismissed, across more than one of the captured views, a minor piece of clutter that should have been cleared before calling the screen state final.
